decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach to the mallet; adjust grasp orientation to its current near-vertical image direction. Right arm remains parked.
Orient the left gripper downward with jaws across the handle and approach its lower shaft. Grasp height and alignment will be checked from the wrist view.
Fine-align to the shaft seen right of wrist center, lowering to grasp height while keeping the elbow-up posture.
Center the shaft between the left jaws and close fully; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Lift the closed grasp clear of the table and start rotating the mallet toward the keys, retaining the left elbow-up configuration.
Carry the visibly retained mallet toward the first red key while rotating its tip rightward, keeping the left wrist in the left workspace and the tip elevated.
Finish orienting the mallet diagonally rightward and align above the first red bar; keep clearance before the strike.
Lower toward the first red key with a small forward correction; inspect mallet-tip contact before lifting and advancing.
Strike the leftmost red key and lift the mallet 5 cm vertically before moving to the next key.
Advance above the second, orange key, strike vertically, and lift 5 cm before continuing left to right.
Move to the third yellow key at clearance, strike, then lift 5 cm with the mallet held closed.
Advance to the fourth green key, strike vertically, and lift 5 cm before advancing again.
Strike the fifth, light-blue key after moving at clearance; lift 5 cm afterward while retaining the mallet.
Advance to the sixth dark-blue key, strike vertically, and lift 5 cm before moving farther right.
Strike the seventh purple key and lift 5 cm afterward; keep the left wrist on its own side and the right arm parked.
Strike the eighth, rightmost magenta key and lift 5 cm to finish the left-to-right sequence; check the resulting observation.
